To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the SE performance of massive MIMO is affected by space constraints and that ZF and MMSe receivers are the preferred choice in this scenario.

(a) MRC is sub-optimal for space constrained MIMO topologies, (b) ZF and MMSEE can still deliver an SE that grows with the number of BS-antennas, (c) the SE performance of ZF and MMSEC is affected by the total space available for the antenna array.
(i) MRC is non-optimal, (ii) the SE of ZF is lower bounded by the SE of the MRC, and (iii) the SE of MMSE is lower bounded by a function of the SE of ZFs.

the fundamental SE limits of space-constrained multi-user massive MIMO systems, and can serve as a reference for future research and practical system design.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the space-constrained massive-MIMO systems can deliver a very high sum SE, which is only slightly smaller than the one of the unconstrained case.
space-constrained massive-MIMO systems can still achieve an increasing SE as long as the total space available for the antenna array is large enough.
space-constrained massive-MIMO systems with a large enough number of users can still provide an increasing sum SE with the number of antennas.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SE of MRC receiver decreases when the number of antennas increases in a fixed total area.
space constraints can be overcome by increasing the number of BS antenna elements.
, in space-constrained massive multi-antenna setups, the ZF and MMEE receivers can be used to improve the sum SE performance as compared to MRC.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, while space-constrained massive multiple-input multiple output (MIMO) is a viable solution for the deployment of 5G systems, the use of ZF and MMSEE receivers is essential to fully exploit the potential of massive MIMO.
, even for a fixed total space, the SE of a space-constrained massive-MIMO system increases with the number of antennas.
space-constrained massive-MIMO systems can still deliver high SE performance if the number of users is sufficiently small.
